description: We’re a three-person team combining coding, design, and science communication. We built KiviScope to help first-time skywatchers explore real NASA SPHEREx images. Choose a patch of sky, flip between dates, and record whether a dot moved, changed brightness, or disappeared from view. Our roster is set.
summary:
We made KiviScope for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. It’s a website for looking for moving objects in NASA’s infrared images. Pick a place to look and check it on two dates. Flip back and forth and the sky stays put.

A distant object looks like any other dot in one picture. Put a circle where you saw it on each date. “Not sure” is also an option. We save the date and image number for each picture. Two people can mark the same spot and compare what they saw.

There is a lot of sky for one person to examine. With KiviScope, different people can each check a small patch. Then they can go back to the places where somebody saw a possible change. We added a 3D collection so people have something to come back for. Save observations and you can unlock models of real objects.
details:
We made a website that lets you check a patch of sky on two dates. Enter coordinates or start with a place like Barnard’s Star. We pull the pictures from the NASA/IPAC SPHEREx archive. The two pictures go on the same sky grid. Flip back and forth and the sky stays put. Put a circle where you saw the source on each date.

You only need a browser. We made practice examples so you can get the hang of it. We save the date and image number for each picture. Two people can mark the same spot and compare what they saw. That means someone can help check a little of the survey and leave something useful for the next person.

We wrote the site in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The server uses Python and Flask. Astropy reads the coordinates in the FITS files. We use NumPy and SciPy to work with the pixels. A dot can seem to vanish if part of the picture is missing. We shade that part. We also check the wavelengths before comparing brightness.

We wanted people to keep looking. You earn points when you save. Use the points to collect real objects like Ceres. We made a place to display them in 3D, called My Universe.

This project will give us a better understanding of our universe and explore its depths. It is extremely simple to use and user friendly in genral.
